description:
Two loose ends from fz-f98.24, both about tests knowing things they should be
told.

## 1. A duplicated coverage predicate that will drift

`tests/fz2_cli.rs::coverage_environment` re-derives
`aot_link::coverage_env_present` -- the same four variables (`CARGO_LLVM_COV`,
`LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`, and coverage mentions in `RUSTFLAGS` /
`CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`). The integration test observes `fz2` as a subprocess
and cannot call the crate-private original, so it guesses what fz2 will decide.

Preferred fix DELETES the duplicate rather than sharing it: have the test assert
what fz2 ACTUALLY DECIDED from its own `resolve_runtime_archive` telemetry span,
which already carries `source`, instead of predicting the decision from the
environment. That follows [[feedback_tests_use_production_paths]] and removes
the coupling entirely.

Sharing the predicate (making it `pub(crate)` plus a test-support seam) is the
fallback if the telemetry cannot express the invariant.

## 2. The documented local gate is not what CI runs

`cargo test --lib` plus the fixture matrix is what everything in this epic was
gated on. CI runs `cargo test --tests` over EVERY target, and `fz2_cli` and
`aot_variadic_open` were outside the local gate entirely. That is how a
pre-existing `fz2_cli` failure survived a 14-PR stack unnoticed, hidden behind
cargo's fail-fast:

    lib fails    -> matrix never runs
    matrix fails -> fz2_cli never runs

Two of those layers were only discovered by fixing the layer above.

Write the real gate down wherever the contributor-facing gate lives, including
that the coverage-sensitive targets need a `CARGO_LLVM_COV=1` pass -- neither
defect in fz-f98.24 reproduced without it.

## Checks

- `tests/fz2_cli.rs` has no copy of the coverage predicate.
- `cargo test --test fz2_cli` passes with AND without `CARGO_LLVM_COV=1`.
- The gate documentation names every test target and the coverage pass.
title: Delete the duplicated coverage predicate, and document the gate CI actually runs
